about: The Collect of the Sixth Sunday after Epiphany in the 1962 Roman Missal, also used when this formulary is resumed after Pentecost. The proper pages print the body and short Per Dominum cue. The full conclusion and Amen are a separate RG115a expansion with declared house orthography.

seg.tr: Grant, we beseech You, almighty God, that, always meditating on what is reasonable, we may accomplish, both in word and in deed, the things that please You. Through our Lord Jesus Christ, Your Son, who lives and reigns with You in the unity of the Holy Spirit, God, forever and ever.

a.g: always meditating on what is reasonable,
we may carry out what is pleasing to You, both in words and in deeds

ex.w012: Plácita here describes the neuter plural things as pleasing to God. The form derives from placeo and can function adjectivally. It does not mean that the things have themselves been pleased.
